COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
AO No. 457 of 2024
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, ACJ
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
(1) Mr. Vinod Tiwari learned counsel for 
the appellant. 
(2) This is an appeal filed under Section 
47 of Guardian and Ward Act, 1890 
challenging the order dated 30.09.2024 
passed by learned Judge, Family Court, 
Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
(3) Learned counsel for the appellant 
submits that there are fair chances of 
amicable settlement between the parties 
and the appellant is ready to restore 
normalcy in the relation and to accept the 
respondent back in the matrimonial home. 
Thus, he submits that efforts can be made 
to bring about a settlement between the 
parties. 
(4) Issue notice to the respondent 
returnable at an early date.
(5) Steps to be taken on or before 
30.12.2024.
(6) List this case on 25.02.2025, on which 
date appellant as well as respondent shall 
appear in person before this Court for 
conciliation. 
(7) Appellant shall deposit a sum of 
₹10,000/- in the Registry to meet the travel 
& other expenses to the respondent for her 
visit to Nainital on the date fixed. (8) Both the parties shall be sent for 
conciliation before the Counsellor attached
at State Legal Services Authority. 
(9) Registry shall send a copy of this order 
along with notice to the respondent so that 
she may be aware about the proposal made 
by the appellant before this Court. 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.)(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, ACJ)
 26.12.2024
Aswal

AO No.457 of 2024
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Vinod Tiwari, learned counsel 
for the appellant.
2. Mr. D.N. Sharma, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
3. In sequel to order dated 26.12.2024, the 
appellant is present while respondent is not 
present before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent submits 
that the date fixed in the matter was 25.02.2025. 
Since the case could not be listed on the said date 
and it has suddenly come on the list today, 
therefore, his client could not remain present 
before the Court. He assures that on the next date 
of listing, his client will remain present. He also 
submits that there are chances of amicable 
settlement between the parties.
5. In such view of the matter, list the matter on 
25.03.2025, on which date, both the parties shall 
appear in person before this Court to explore the 
possibilities of settlement of the dispute.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 
 04.03.2025
